newsitem.title: LIBERIA: Peacekeepers raid more Liberian homes for arms.
newsitem.headline: Peacekeepers raid more Liberian homes for arms.

text.p: Peacekeepers hunting for illegal weapons in Liberia on Sunday raided the homes of relatives of a warlord arrested last week over an arms cache.

Witnesses said the heavily armed troops of the ECOMOG force stormed the homes of Lansanah Kromah, a cabinet minister in the country's interim government and Abe Kromah, chief of staff of the rump of Liberia's former national army.

Peacekeeping tanks moved up close to Abe's home and troops leaped over a high fence and broke into his bedroom. Other units carried out cordon and search operations in nearby homes of former guerrilla commanders.
"They took away the five arms assigned to the ECOMOG guards at my house and seized my side pistol," Abe told Reuters.
Witnesses said troops broke into Lansanah's home later, dug into an old generator room but found no arms.
Both men are related to Alhaji Kromah, one of two warlords at the centre of Liberia's seven-year civil war, who was arrested in a raid on his home on Friday.

Friday's raid yielded a spectacular cache of weapons, including anti-aircraft guns and crateas of explosives. Reporters saw the haul at the force's headquarters where it was transported in three trucks from Kromah's home.

Troops also arrested 40 men said to have been found receiving military training in the home of Kromah, one of three declared contenders for presidential elections due in May to wrap up a delicate regional piece plan on ending the war.
Liberia's warring factions have officially been disbanded and all weapons were supposed to have been surrendered by a January 31 deadline under the peace plan.
An aide to warlord Kromah acknowledged the presence of the arsenal seized at his boss's home on Friday but insisted they had been declared to the Nigerian-led ECOMOG.
General Moses Dah told BBC Africa Service radio in a telephone interview that Kromah had been set up by unnamed enemies he said were bent on destroying his political career.

"The arms were there with their knowledge because there was an inventory of the arms...The CMIO (chief military intelligence officer) of ECOMOG is fully aware of these arms being there," he said, adding that ECOMOG was to have retrieved them to its base.
ECOMOG's Nigerian commander General Victor Malu told a news conference on Friday Kromah could face the law, a prospect that would put his presidential ambitions in jeopardy.
"He will be treated like the other criminals found with illegal weapons," Malu said.
